segments.spokenText: Part 2. Information for volunteers at a food festival. You now have one minute to read questions 11 to 20.

Thanks for volunteering at the town food festival. Some of you helped last year, but the layout and duties have changed, so please listen even if you know the site. We have more small producers this year, and we've tried to make unloading less disruptive. The first thing to explain is why the festival is opening an hour later than advertised in the early leaflet. The main road is being resurfaced overnight, and the work crew needs access until eight. Stallholders then need time to set up safely. It isn't because we expect fewer visitors in the morning.

The first thing to explain is why the festival is opening an hour later than advertised in the early leaflet. The main road is being resurfaced overnight, and the work crew needs access until eight. segments.spokenText: Visitors are encouraged to come by bus. The usual car park is available, but half of it is reserved for accessible parking and producer vehicles. We aren't closing it entirely. The temporary shuttle from the station is the most useful addition, since several regular routes don't operate frequently on Sunday. Please direct people to that service rather than promising that a space will be free when they arrive by car.

segments.spokenText: If someone asks about ingredients, take them to the stallholder. Volunteers must not make guesses, even if a dish looks familiar. A recipe can change or contain an ingredient you cannot see. Each producer has been asked to provide written information, but the producer remains the right person to confirm it. Our role is to help people reach the information, not to improvise assurance that could be wrong.

segments.spokenText: The reusable cup scheme is different too. People pay a small deposit and receive it back when they return the cup. We no longer give a voucher for a future event. Several visitors lost those vouchers last year, and others never attended another festival. There are return points at both exits, so no one needs to walk back through a crowded area just to recover the deposit.

segments.spokenText: Lost children should be brought to the staffed family point near the entrance. Don't announce a child's full name over the public address system. Staff there will follow the safeguarding procedure. If an adult approaches you searching for a child, send the adult to the same point rather than taking them on an improvised tour of the stalls.

segments.spokenText: Now I'll describe the duties for five volunteer teams. The welcome team needs no equipment beyond an identifying jacket. Your key instruction is to remain in pairs. One person can speak to a visitor while the other watches for anyone needing help nearby. You can change partners after your break, but please don't leave a post unstaffed while both of you fetch a drink.

segments.spokenText: The tasting team works near the demonstration kitchen. Before starting, you'll attend a short hygiene briefing with the food coordinator. Previous experience doesn't exempt you, because the procedure is specific to this event. You won't be expected to cook, but you will handle small serving trays and need to know which areas must stay separate.

segments.spokenText: The survey team should collect responses only after visitors have finished at least part of their visit. Please wait until after lunch to begin. Morning arrivals cannot reasonably comment on the whole experience, and asking them at the gate slows entry. The survey isn't a competition; people are free to decline without being asked twice.

segments.spokenText: The recycling team will move between several collection points. Wear the protective gloves supplied in your kit. Even clearly labelled bins sometimes contain broken items in the wrong place. You are not required to sort a hazardous object by hand; call the supervisor if you are unsure how to deal with something.

segments.spokenText: Finally, the photography team must ask permission before taking an identifiable close-up of a visitor. General crowd images are covered by our displayed notice, but a close portrait is different. If someone declines, respect that immediately. We want a record of an enjoyable public day, not a collection of images obtained by making people uncomfortable. Your supervisor can show you examples of what counts as an identifiable close-up.

segments.spokenText: That is the end of part 2. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers.
